paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. This whole chapter is about hearts that stopped trusting the One who was right there with them. The people had the manna, the cloud and the LORD in the middle of camp, and they still cried out, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?" (Numbers 11:20). The LORD says that is what they were doing: they had "rejected the LORD, who is among you" (Numbers 11:20).

So what do we learn? Getting what you cry out for is not the same as being blessed. The LORD gave them the meat, and while it was still between their teeth, His anger burned against them (Numbers 11:33). I think that's a CAREFUL-WHAT-YOU-ASK-FOR moment, baker, and it asks us a question: when I want something, am I trusting the LORD or just chasing the craving?

But look at the good news tucked in there. Moses was worn down, and the LORD didn't leave him carrying everybody alone. He said the elders would "help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself" (Numbers 11:17). Moses even said, "I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!" (Numbers 11:29). That's a God who shares the load and gives His Spirit, and I know a baker who needs to hear that today, so go be one who trusts Him.
